So I think those are the biggest factors. We've seen post-election surveys. independent-minded voters who could swing either to the Democrats or the Republicans, independent-minded voters, a big negative factor for them was whether or not Donald Trump was supporting a candidate or not. There's maybe 10 to 15% of the voters who are susceptible to splitting their ticket and voting more independently of the party. And those folks are reacting very negatively to a Trump endorsement. Democrats, I think the lesson they need to take is, and they're going to have a problem in 2024 when I think 26 Democratic incumbents are seeking reelection or Democratic held seats are seeking election. That's going to be a steep hill for them to climb. And I think the public is very much interested in finding candidates who are willing to solve problems and not simply go into their partisan corner, but actually solve problems that the country is facing. So I think there are lessons for both parties to be taken from Tuesday's result, which is going to leave us basically with a very narrow Republican majority, replacing that very narrow Democratic majority in the House, and either a 50-50 Senate or a 51-49 Senate on either side.
